messages.content: Draft an HHVC Transaction page for bed bug complaints. Use this exact heading format: PAGE NAME:, PAGE TYPE:, PRIMARY USER:. Include clear next steps and mention 311.

judgeSamples.output:
# Bed Bug Complaint Draft — Karl CMS Transaction Page

---

**PAGE NAME:** Report a Bed Bug Problem in Your Home or Building

**PAGE TYPE:** Transaction

**PRIMARY USER:** San Francisco renter, tenant, or building occupant who has discovered bed bugs and needs to file a complaint with the City

---

## What This Page Does

This is a **Transaction page** — it serves as the entry point into a City service and must be actionable. The resident is trying to *do something* (file a complaint), not just read information.

> Per the Karl editor guide on choosing a content type: a Transaction page is the right choice here because the user must take action with the City.
> 📖 [https://sfdigitalservices.gitbook.io/karl-sf.gov-editor-help-center/using-karl-the-cms/content-types/choosing-a-content-type](https://sfdigitalservices.gitbook.io/karl-sf.gov-editor-help-center/using-karl-the-cms/content-types/choosing-a-content-type)

---

## DRAFT PAGE CONTENT

---

### Intro / Lead Text

**Report a bed bug problem in your home or building**

If you have bed bugs in your rental unit, your landlord is required to address the infestation. If your landlord has not responded or refused to act, you can file a complaint with the City.

---

### What You'll Need Before You Start

- Your address and unit number
- The date you first noticed bed bugs
- Documentation that you notified your landlord (texts, emails, or written notice — if you have it)
- Your contact information

---

### How to File a Complaint

**Option 1 — Report online or by phone through 311**

The fastest way to report a bed bug complaint is through **SF 311**, San Francisco's non-emergency City services line.

- 📞 **Call 311** (or 415-701-2311 from outside SF)
- 💻 **Submit online at** [sf311.org](https://sf311.org)
- 📱 **Use the SF311 app** (available on iOS and Android)

311 will route your complaint to the **Department of Building Inspection (DBI)** or the **San Francisco Department of Public Health (SFDPH)**, depending on the nature of your complaint.

---

**Option 2 — File directly with the Department of Building Inspection**

You can also contact DBI directly to report housing code violations related to bed bugs.

- Visit the **Complaint Intake Counter** at 49 South Van Ness Avenue
- Call DBI's complaint line
- Submit a complaint through the DBI online portal

---

**Option 3 — Contact the Department of Public Health**

If you believe the infestation poses a public health risk or affects multiple units, contact SFDPH's **Housing and Environmental Health** section.

---

### What Happens After You File

1. **Your complaint is logged** — 311 or DBI assigns a case number. Save this for your records.
2. **An inspector is assigned** — A housing inspector will contact you to schedule a visit.
3. **Inspection takes place** — The inspector documents the conditions in your unit.
4. **Landlord is notified** — If violations are found, the landlord receives a formal notice to correct the problem.
5. **Follow-up** — If the landlord does not comply, further enforcement action may be taken.

---

### Supporting Information

> ℹ️ *In Karl, the sections below are built as **Supporting information** on the Transaction page. The heading "Supporting information" does not appear on the live public page — only your custom headings show.*
> 📖 [https://sfdigitalservices.gitbook.io/karl-sf.gov-editor-help-center/using-karl-the-cms/content-types/building-a-page-by-content-type/transaction/supporting-information-on-a-transaction-page](https://sfdigitalservices.gitbook.io/karl-sf.gov-editor-help-center/using-karl-the-cms/content-types/building-a-page-by-content-type/transaction/supporting-information-on-a-transaction-page)

---

#### Your rights as a tenant

Under San Francisco law, landlords must maintain rental units free of pest infestations, including bed bugs. Bed bugs are considered a **habitability issue** under the San Francisco Housing Code. Your landlord cannot retaliate against you for filing a complaint.

If you face harassment or retaliation after reporting, contact the **San Francisco Rent Board** or a tenant rights organization.

---

#### What landlords are required to do

Landlords must:
- Respond promptly when notified of a bed bug infestation
- Hire a licensed pest control professional
- Not rent a unit they know has an active bed bug infestation
- Provide advance notice before entering to inspect or treat

---

#### Tips while you wait for an inspection

- Do not throw away furniture without documenting it first (photograph everything)
- Place bed bug interceptors under bed legs to help confirm activity
- Wash and dry bedding on high heat
- Avoid moving items from the infested unit to other rooms or units, as this can spread the infestation

---

#### If you live in a hotel or SRO

Residents of single-room occupancy hotels (SROs) and residential hotels have the same rights. Contact the **City's SRO Collaborative** or file through 311 as described above.

---

### Related Pages

> ℹ️ *In Karl, add these as **Related pages** in the right-hand column of the Transaction page. Only Transaction, Information, Campaign, and Topic pages can be tagged as Related.*
> 📖 [https://sfdigitalservices.gitbook.io/karl-sf.gov-editor-help-center/using-karl-the-cms/components/related](https://sfdigitalservices.gitbook.io/karl-sf.gov-editor

judgeSamples.output:
# Mold Prevention for Tenants

---

**PAGE NAME:** Mold Prevention for Tenants
**PAGE TYPE:** Information
**PRIMARY USER:** Renters who want to prevent mold growth in their home

---

## About this page

This Information page gives renters practical steps to prevent mold. It does not ask the user to take action with the City, so Information is the right content type. If a user needs to report mold or file a complaint, a separate Transaction page should handle that.

> 📖 **Content type guidance:** [Choosing a content type](https://sfdigitalservices.gitbook.io/karl-sf.gov-editor-help-center/using-karl-the-cms/content-types/choosing-a-content-type) — *Information: non-actionable reference; use Transaction if the user must do something with the City.*

---

## Draft page content

---

### Page name
Mold Prevention for Tenants

---

### Description (shown in search results and link previews)
Learn how to prevent mold in your rental home and protect your health.

---

### Body content

---

#### What is mold?

Mold is a fungus that grows in damp or wet areas. It can appear as black, green, or white spots. Mold can make you sick, especially if you have asthma or allergies.

---

#### Why renters should care

- Mold spreads quickly in small spaces
- It can damage walls, ceilings, and furniture
- It can cause breathing problems, coughing, and skin irritation
- Landlords are required to keep your home free from mold hazards

---

#### How to prevent mold in your home

**Control moisture**
- Wipe up spills and leaks right away
- Dry wet surfaces within 24 to 48 hours
- Fix dripping faucets and report leaks to your landlord

**Improve airflow**
- Open windows when the weather allows
- Use exhaust fans in the bathroom and kitchen while cooking or showering
- Keep furniture a few inches away from walls

**Reduce humidity**
- Use a dehumidifier if your home feels damp
- Hang laundry outside or use a dryer — not indoors — when possible
- Keep indoor humidity below 60 percent

**Clean regularly**
- Clean bathrooms and kitchens with mold-killing products
- Check under sinks and around pipes often
- Throw away items that have mold that cannot be cleaned

---

#### When to tell your landlord

Tell your landlord right away if you see:

- Mold or dark spots on walls, ceilings, or floors
- A musty smell that does not go away
- Water leaks, flooding, or condensation on windows

Your landlord must fix mold problems that affect your health and safety. Keep a copy of any complaints you make in writing.

---

#### When to get help

If your landlord does not fix the problem, you have options:

- Contact the **San Francisco Department of Building Inspection (DBI)**
- Reach out to a tenant rights organization
- Call **311** to report a housing complaint

---

### Part of (Transaction page link)

> 📖 Per Karl CMS guidance, this Information page should be linked to exactly one Transaction page using the **Part of** component:
> [Part of on an Information page](https://sfdigitalservices.gitbook.io/karl-sf.gov-editor-help-center/using-karl-the-cms/content-types/building-a-page-by-content-type/information/part-of-on-an-information-page)

**Suggested Transaction page to link:**
*Report a Housing Code Violation* — or whichever Transaction page covers housing complaint filing on SF.gov.

---

### Related pages

No Related pages are added to Information pages directly. Related pages (Transaction, Information, Campaign, or Topic) are managed on the Transaction page side.

> 📖 [Related component guidance](https://sfdigitalservices.gitbook.io/karl-sf.gov-editor-help-center/using-karl-the-cms/components/related) — *Only Transaction, Information, Campaign, and Topic pages can be tagged as Related.*

---

## Editor notes

| Field | Entry |
|---|---|
| Page name | Mold Prevention for Tenants |
| Page type | Information |
| Primary user | Renters who want to prevent mold in their home |
| Part of (Transaction) | Report a Housing Code Violation *(confirm exact page name)* |
| Reading level target | 6th grade or below |
| Status | Draft — needs SME review before publishing |

output.summary: Transaction type is correct and 311 is referenced, but the page lacks actionable first-person language, uses passive voice and hidden verbs, omits tenant responsibilities, and the parent Topic name does not match Karl standards.
passed: Page type is valid Karl content type: Transaction
Components used (Title, Description, What to know, What to do) are all valid Karl components
311 reference is present in What to do section
Plain language: mostly simple vocabulary appropriate for 5th-6th grade level
warnings: Title is not action-oriented or in first person — change 'Report bed bugs in your apartment' to 'Report bed bugs in my apartment' or 'I need to report bed bugs'
What to know section leads with background context instead of actionable information — reorder to prioritize what user needs to do first
Sentence 'We inspect for signs of infestation' contains hidden verb construction — use active form 'We look for signs of infestation' or clarify timeline

Paragraph length warning: What to know section is 2 sentences but lacks user context; What to do is 2 sentences but should explain tenant responsibilities per https://sfdigitalservices.gitbook.io/karl-sf.gov-editor-help-center/using-karl-the-cms/content-types/building-a-page-by-content-type/transaction
failed: Missing first-person 'you' language in body content — body should say 'You can call 311' or 'You should keep records', not use imperative without addressing reader directly
Passive voice found: 'so we can inspect your home' — rewrite as active construction: 'so the City can send an inspector'
Hidden verb: 'file a complaint' — use simpler form 'call 311 to report bed bugs'
Tenant responsibilities are completely absent — Transaction pages must include what tenants must or should do; add guidance on preparing the apartment, providing access, or documenting the problem
System Relationships Parent name does not match Karl standard — change 'Healthy housing and pests' to 'Healthy Housing and Vector Control' to align with SF.gov Topic naming

PAGE NAME: Report bed bugs in your apartment
PAGE TYPE: Transaction
PRIMARY USER: Tenant

SECTION: Report bed bugs now
Call 311 to report bed bugs in your home.

ACTION LINK: Call 311

SECTION: Why you need to act fast
Bed bugs spread between units quickly. DPH inspects health and pest issues. We aim to respond within 48 hours of your report.

CALLOUT: DPH handles bed bug and pest inspections. For structural repairs, contact DBI.

SECTION: What tenants need to do
Prepare your home before the inspector arrives. Your landlord must also be notified of the problem.

SECTION: Contact us
Call 311 to report bed bugs or ask questions. You can also visit SF.gov/311.

---

**DUPLICATION RISKS:**
- "Report bed bugs" may overlap with an existing 311 service page. Check before publishing.
- Tenant responsibility language may duplicate content in the HHVC Tenant Hub overview page.

**KARL CMS NOTES:**
- Content Title (internal): HHVC - Tenant Hub - Report Bed Bugs
- Service Title (public H1): Report bed bugs in your apartment
- Summary: Call 311 to report bed bugs in your home so we can inspect within 48 hours.
- CTA Button Label: Call 311

judgeSamples.output:
PAGE NAME: Fix trash and pest problems in shared buildings
PAGE TYPE: Transaction
PRIMARY USER: Property owner

SECTION: What you need to do first
Call 311 to get city support before starting cleanup.

[Action Link: Call 311]
[Action Link: 311.sf.gov]

SECTION: What owners must do
You must respond to tenant complaints and coordinate cleanup of trash and pest problems in your building.

SECTION: What we inspect
We inspect shared areas of buildings for trash buildup and pest problems. This includes hallways, trash rooms, and shared outdoor spaces. Inspections follow SF Health Code Article 11.

SECTION: Who handles what
[Callout]
DPH (Department of Public Health) handles health and cleanliness problems — like trash pileups and pest issues. DBI (Department of Building Inspection) handles structural and safety problems — like broken walls or unsafe stairs. This page is about DPH issues only.
[End Callout]

SECTION: Tenant and owner responsibilities
**Owners must:**
- Respond quickly to tenant complaints
- Set up and coordinate cleanup
- Keep shared spaces free of trash and pests

**Tenants must:**
- Report trash and pest problems right away
- Keep their own unit clean

SECTION: Contact
[Action Link: Call 311]
[Action Link: 311.sf.gov]

Office: SF Department of Public Health, 49 South Van Ness Ave, San Francisco, CA 94103

---
DUPLICATION RISKS: Check existing SF.gov pages for "report trash problems" and "pest control rental housing" to avoid overlap with this Transaction page.
